pairs.locus: Otto of Freising (Rahewin), Gesta Friderici IV.77 (acclamation of Pope Victor at St Peter's)
pairs.question: Audite, cives Romani et coetus rei publicae! Secunda feria pater noster Adrianus mortuus est, et proximo sequenti sabbato domnus Octavianus cardinalis Sanctae Ceciliae in Romanum pontificem electus et inmantatus est et in kathedra beati Petri collocatus est et papa Victor est nominatus. Placet vobis?
pairs.derivation: The scriniarius proclaims the election to the people and ends with a genuine interrogative 'Placet vobis?'; the clergy and people answer 'Placet'. Per whole-speech-as-question guidance the entire proclamation is quoted verbatim as the question (the narrative preceding 'Placet vobis?' supplies the referent for the assent). Dropped the framing 'Tunc scriniarius... clamavit ad populum, dicens:' and 'Respondit magna voce clerus et populus:', and stripped the curly-quote speech delimiters. The immediately following repeated indirect acclamations ('Secunda et tercia vice interrogatus populus, si placeret...') are not quoted, since they are reported indirectly.

pairs.locus: Otto of Freising (Rahewin), Gesta Friderici IV.77 (clerics of San Crisogono question their cardinal)
pairs.question: Omnes clerici vadunt ad pedes domni papae; quid faciemus et nos?
pairs.derivation: The clerics of the cardinalia of San Crisogono ask their cardinal a real interrogative ('quid faciemus et nos?', with the preceding clause supplying its setup), and he answers directly. Dropped the framing 'dixerunt se... accessisse ad cardinalem suum... et interrogasse eum, dicentes:' and 'Qui respondit:', and stripped the curly-quote speech delimiters. Answer is the single contiguous reply sentence.
